messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Elevated 5xx rate observed for runtime-serving. Metric: kv_cache_error_rate ↑ 18% in last 3m. Affected routes: /v1/chat, /v1/generate. Severity: P1. thread_ts=1783104560
ana (eng-runtime): i'm seeing a correlated spike in continuous-batching latency and KV cache size. looks like cache reuse is reusing stale entries across requests. logs show repeated seq_offset mismatches. paging @ryan-oncall
ryan-oncall: on it. joining R6. any immediate customer-facing impacts?
maria-sre: some customers on Dedicated are seeing inference errors (wrong continuations) and elevated latency > 2s p50 -> 600ms->2s. CS reported 2 enterprise tenants with misaligned outputs. @emily-cs please confirm which tenants and severity
emily-cs: confirmed: AcmeAnalytics and GreenBank reported malformed outputs to their QA pipelines. both paused traffic. labeled as "major user impact". they want ETA.
devin (eng-platform): hypothesis: KV cache reuse logic introduced in last deploy (2026-03-12) incorrectly keys cache by {model,shard} only, missing request seq_base -> cross-request leakage when using continuous batching. reproducer created locally.
nana (eng-runtime): logs show entries like: `kv_key={model:gptx,shard:3}` reused while client_seq_base=120 then later client_seq_base=80 -> seq_offset calc wrong -> stale KV served.
sre_lead: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable KV reuse globally (fast but cost increase), 2) rollback last deploy (safest if small change), 3) hotfix to include seq_base in key generation (safer but needs rollout). thoughts?
ryan-oncall: what's the blast radius for a rollback? would that affect other unrelated runtime fixes?
devin (eng-platform): the deploy touched kernel selection and batching. rollback would revert kernel perf tweaks but should restore correct cache behavior. estimated 10m for rollback, 5m validation after.
maria-sre: we should also consider a toggle to turn off continuous-batching at the route level for high-risk customers as an intermediate mitigation.
nana (eng-runtime): i can flip an emergency feature-flag to disable KV reuse for all hosted traffic now. command: `/ff set runtime.kv_reuse false --env prod` — will take ~45s to propagate. downside: token cost up ~15-30%.
ryan-oncall: do it. notify customers.
nana (eng-runtime): executed `/ff set runtime.kv_reuse false --env prod` — propagation started. watching metrics.
incident-bot: Feature flag change detected: runtime.kv_reuse=false by ana (eng-runtime). All regions.
nana (eng-runtime): metrics moving — kv_cache_error_rate dropping, 5xx tail decreasing. latency p50 slowly stabilizing. turning on tighter logging for repro traces.
emily-cs: informed AcmeAnalytics and GreenBank of mitigation and temporary cost/perf impact. they asked for status page update. I posted an update to status.redwood.ai/incidents/1783104560
ryan-oncall: good. next: create an incident ticket, assign eng-runtime to root cause and eng-platform for rollback/hotfix decision. assemble a small war room for RCA.
nana (eng-runtime): small reproducer snippet (for the RCA thread) — shows reuse across seq offsets:
```
# simplified repro
req1: client_id=A seq_base=100 tokens=[..] -> cache stored key=(model=gptx,shard=3) value=(kv_blob, stored_seq_base=100)
req2: client_id=B seq_base=80  tokens=[..] -> cache hit for key=(model=gptx,shard=3) but stored_seq_base=100 -> applied as if seq_base=80 -> output shifted
```

maria-sre: captures in logs: `WARN runtime.kv_cache: seq_offset_mismatch stored=100 incoming=80 key=model=gptx/shard=3 trace_id=...` repeated for ~3k requests during spike window.
devin (eng-platform): preparing a minimal hotfix to include `seq_base` in cache key. patch looks small but needs careful rollout (keyspace change will disable old entries). propose canary to 10% then ramp.
sre_lead: timelines: (A) FF disable runtime.kv_reuse — done. (B) hotfix PR in ~30m, canary 10% -> 1h monitoring, full rollout if green. (C) rollback option reserved if hotfix introduces perf regressions.
ryan-oncall: assign incident ticket to ENG-INC-7891. @devin PR and @ana coordinate canary. maria, you handle monitoring and hooking alerts for seq_offset warnings. emily, keep customers informed. I'm taking command until 18:30 then handoff to maria.
emily-cs: posted customer update and personalized emails to the two impacted tenants. both acknowledged and will continue paused testing until green.
nana (eng-runtime): PR opened: `platform#4521` — hotfix adds seq_base to cache key and increments cache version. test harness shows repro prevented. rolling canary to 10% now.
incident-bot: Canary rollout started for platform#4521 -> cohort=10% regions: us-east-1,eu-west-1.
devin (eng-platform): canary metrics: no seq_offset warnings in canary cohort after 5m. latency stable.
maria-sre: monitoring shows seq warnings down 92% overall. still seeing rare decreases where legacy entries evicted slowly. continuing to watch.
ryan-oncall: update ETA for customers?
emily-cs: tell them we expect full resolution within 90 minutes pending canary — will update if anything changes.
sre_lead: postmortem action items (initial): - make seq_base part of canonical cache key in runtime (owner: eng-runtime) - add unit tests for cross-request KV reuse scenarios (owner: eng-platform) - add alert for seq_offset_mismatch (owner: eng-sre) - document runbook step for emergency FF flip (owner: eng-sre)
nana (eng-runtime): canary ramp to 50% complete. no regressions seen.
nana (eng-runtime): canary ramp to 100% complete. KV reuse hotfix in prod.
incident-bot: Change: platform#4521 rolled to 100% by ana (eng-runtime).
ryan-oncall: great work. closing immediate mitigation. creating follow-up meeting for RCA deep-dive at 14:00 UTC tomorrow. handing command to maria for oncall until 22:00.
maria-sre: taking over oncall. i'll monitor for 2 hours then handback.
emily-cs: final customer update sent: issue mitigated with config and hotfix, we will follow up with RCA and timeline for any potential cost/latency changes. customers appreciated the quick turnaround.
ryan-oncall: thanks everyone. file incident report and include logs for `seq_offset_mismatch`.
sre_lead: incident severity will be updated to Sev3 post-mitigation. schedule RCA and assign owners.
nana (eng-runtime): note for postmortem: we also need to evaluate cache TTLs and eviction behavior — old entries persisted longer than expected and contributed to cross-request hits. adding to action list.
incident-bot: Incident ENG-INC-7891 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
